evidence.curator_note: Equation 8.55, UPPER 'alpha' branch off the ring-opened distonic ion: the second half of the stepwise retro-Diels-Alder. Radical site C4 -> forming pi C4=C5 (the expelled neutral ethylene); one electron of the sigma C5-C6 -> that forming pi; the second electron of C5-C6 -> C6, so the charge-bearing four-carbon fragment leaves as the diene radical cation ('+ C2H4' is written next to it on the page). Book draws 0 arc(s) on this branch (only the 'alpha'-labelled arrow, the bracketed diene+. and '+ C2H4'); moves <1,2,3> are curator-supplied hooks required for electron balance, none of them drawn. The text above the scheme motivates the branch: 'This retro-Diels-Alder reaction now produces (Equation 8.55) a resonance stabilized diene+. in place of the olefin+. product of Equation 8.48, lowering the IE of the corresponding neutral by ~1 eV.' RESONANCE (convention C): the book draws the product as the fully conjugated butadiene radical cation CH2=CH-CH=CH2 in brackets with '+.'; the arrows as encoded produce the localised form .CH2-CH(+)-CH=CH2 (charge stays on C1, where the drawn allyl cation was localised in record IMS8-EQ8.55a; the odd electron lands on C6). Both are localisation/resonance forms of the same delocalised C4H6+. ion - a radical cation cannot be written with two intact pi bonds in RDKit-parseable SMILES.

rule_index.json 'by_equation' has NO entry for 8.55; no MOD rule variable is cross-linked. CHECKED, AND THE ONE RULE THAT DOES MATCH DISAGREES WITH THE BOOK: IMS_4_30 ('Ring spaltung generell', eq 4.30, DFS '[C.]1[C]2[C]3[C+]4[C]5{=}[C]6>>[C.]1[C+]2.[C]3{=}[C]4[C]5{=}[C]6') matches this exact precursor - RDKit substructure test of its LHS as SMARTS '[#6;v3;+0]-[#6]-[#6]-[#6;v3;+1]-[#6]=[#6]' against [CH2:3]=[CH:2][CH+:1][CH2:6][CH2:5][CH2:4] gives 1 match (C4-C5-C6-C1-C2-C3) - and it cleaves the SAME sigma bond (C5-C6), but it distributes the products the other way round: charge and odd electron stay on the two-carbon fragment (ionised ethylene .CH2-CH2+, C2H4+., m/z 28) and butadiene leaves NEUTRAL, i.e. the complement of the branch drawn in 8.55, whose ion is C4H6+. (80% on this page). The 7-carbon rules IMS_4_31_alpha2 and IMS_4_32_ind do encode this alpha-cleavage geometry correctly, but they cannot match here: RDKit substructure test of their LHS '[#6]-[#6;v3;+0]-[#6]-[#6]-[#6;v3;+1]-[#6]=[#6]' against the same precursor gives 0 matches (they require an extra C substituent on the terminal radical carbon). No MOD rule reproduces the book's 8.55 upper branch.

The page prints the abundance in the running text below the scheme: 'the C4H6+. abundance from cyclohexene is 80%, versus 25% from methylenecyclopentane and <=5% from methylcyclopentenes' -> relative_intensity 0.80. observed_mz 54.0464 is the curator-computed monoisotopic m/z of C4H6+. (electron-mass corrected); the page prints no m/z, and no ionisation conditions are restated on this page (70 eV EI is the chapter default, not a page statement).
